On the company's own capex definition, computed from reported figures by adding finance lease principal payments to purchases of property and equipment, the capital expenditures as the company defines them ($72.22 billion) is above the range[4]. Because the 2025 fiscal year has ended and the reported figures are within or above the promised range, the status is Delivered.

explanation.text: Meta Platforms said in its 10-Q filed 2025-10-30 that "We anticipate making capital expenditures of approximately $70 billion to $72 billion in 2025 to support our core business and AI efforts, and expect significant capital expenditures growth in 2026."[1] The FY2025 10-K reports “$69.69 billion of purchases of property and equipment”[2], and compared by code with the promised range of $70 billion to $72 billion, the capex for the fiscal year ended 2025-12-31 ($69.69 billion) is below the range; it does not reach the low end.[3] The company's 8-K filed 2026-01-28 reports, as company-reported, capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, were $22.14 billion and $72.22 billion for the fourth quarter and full year 2025, respectively.[4] Because the promise does not say which definition it uses, this capex figure is above the range and reaches its low end, so the status is Delivered.
